newsitem.title: USA: Convicted US derivatives salesman could face 5 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Convicted US derivatives salesman could face 5 yrs.

text.p: Bond salesman Kenneth Schulte could face up to five years in prison after being found guilty in U.S. District Court this week of fraud, federal officials said Thursday.

Schulte, 38, of Del Ray Beach, Fla., is believed to be the first person convicted for selling risky derivatives to local governments, said Peggy Kramer, a lawyer with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission in Chicago.
A jury found him guilty on six felony mail, wire and securities fraud charges, First Assistant U.S. Attorney William Edwards of Ohio's northern district said.
John Gibbons, Schulte's lawyer, said Schulte plans to appeal the conviction. He is scheduled to be sentenced May 6.
After nearly two weeks' testimony in U.S. District Court, a jury deliberated for two days.

Edwards said Schulte misled several local governments and school systems in Ohio into buying risky interest-only securities. Hardest hit was the city of Painesville, near Cleveland, which lost $4.6 million when interest rates fell.
"He misled them," Edwards said. "He led them to believe the principal was protected (by the federal government) when actually it was not."

In a separate civil action, the SEC is seeking to have Schulte barred from the securities industry, Kramer said. Earlier, in another SEC civil action, a federal judge ordered Schulte to return nearly $400,000 in commissions he received from the sales, she said.
